Emily — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We can support a short-term burst and then reconcile to a longer-term commit, but we'll need to align on the measurable utilization thresholds and credit mechanics.

Proposed approach from sales/CS side:
1) Short burst: reserve 8x A100-class GPUs in a "burst pool" for 8 weeks starting 2026-08-15. Include automated autoscale down to 0 for non-peak hours to conserve cost.
2) Commit path: if average week-over-week GPU utilization across the 8-week window stays >= 55% on the burst fleet, BlueHealth can convert up to 6 GPUs into a 12-month reserved tranche with a pro-rated credit for the burst period.
3) Fallback: if utilization < 30% after the 8 weeks, offer a 40% credit on the committed price for the first quarter or a 60% one-time credit applied to invoices (open to negotiation).

I'll loop in Karthik for feasibility and sizing implications. Monica, please prepare an initial pricing schedule and a short SOW outlining the timeline.

Thanks,
Rishi

Emily / team — technical notes and constraints from infra: happy to support but want to be explicit about fragmentation, model placement, and kernel warm-up. A few things to consider:

- Fleet mix: we suggest using 8x A100 40GB (or equivalent rdms) with pinned model variants for the burst. Mixing different GPU types increases scheduling tail latency.
- Autoscale config: configure continuous batching with a 50ms max batch delay and prefix caching to reduce cold-start token cost. During peak we expect per-GPU throughput ~600 tokens/s for your smallest seq len; for long sequences that'll drop — we need your sequence-length distribution.
- Scheduling: recommend a dedicated reservation + a small shared burst pool (2x GPUs) to handle overlapping noise from other customers if you prefer lower cost. Otherwise purely dedicated is simplest for latency SLAs.
- Rollout window: 24–48 hour ramp to warm kernels and KV caches. Expect first 6–12 hours of slightly elevated latency as caches populate.

I'll produce an internal cost estimate for 8 weeks (reserved gpu-hour pricing + 10% engineering runbook surcharge) and a tracked metric list we need from BlueHealth (avg GPU utilization, p95 latency, median token time, failed request rate).

Karthik
Staff Infrastructure Engineer (Serving Runtime)
Redwood Inference

- Short burst: 8 GPUs (A100-40) reserved 2026-08-15 -> 2026-10-10 (8 weeks + weekend buffer). Estimated cost: $164,800 pre-credit.
- Commit conversion: if >= 55% avg GPU utilization over 8 weeks, BlueHealth may convert up to 6 GPUs into a 12-month reserved commitment at a 28% discount vs on-demand. Credit mechanics: pro-rate the unused portion of the burst and apply as a credit to the first month of the reservation.
- Low utilization protection: if < 30% avg utilization, apply a one-time invoice credit equal to 40% of the burst invoice.
- Operational runbook: includes warm-up checklist, rollback steps, and a dedicated Slack channel we will create.

Attachments: proposal_reservation_schedule_v1.xlsx, SOW-dedicated-deployment-v2.pdf
